Miso is a traditional Japanese fermented paste made primarily from soybeans, salt, and kōji mold, used as a fundamental seasoning. Its history in Japan stretches back to prehistoric times, evolving from early Chinese fermented soy foods and becoming a dietary staple by the Kamakura period. The flavor, color, and texture of miso vary widely based on ingredients like rice or barley, fermentation time, and regional production techniques, leading to classifications such as white, red, and mixed miso. While industrial production now dominates, traditional homemade versions played a crucial historical role in nutrition and local economies.
